mercury: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun
venus: The hottest planet, wrapped in thick clouds; the "morning star"
earth: The only planet known to have life
mars: The red planet, home of Olympus Mons
jupiter: The largest planet, with the Great Red Spot
saturn: The planet with the most famous rings
uranus: The ice giant that spins on its side
neptune: The farthest planet, with the fastest winds
ceres: The largest object in the asteroid belt
pluto: Demoted from planet to dwarf planet in 2006
haumea: An egg-shaped dwarf planet that spins every four hours
makemake: A dwarf planet named after the Rapa Nui creator god, found around Easter 2005
eris: The most massive dwarf planet, named after the goddess of discord
io: The most volcanically active body in the solar system, orbiting the largest planet
europa: Icy moon of the largest planet, with an ocean underneath
ganymede: The largest moon in the solar system
callisto: Heavily cratered outer large moon of the largest planet
mimas: Small moon of the ringed planet with a giant crater that makes it look like the Death Star
enceladus: Moon of the ringed planet that sprays water geysers from its south pole
tethys: Mid-sized moon of the ringed planet with the giant canyon Ithaca Chasma
dione: Moon of the ringed planet with bright ice cliffs
rhea: Second-largest moon of the ringed planet
titan: Largest moon of the ringed planet, with a thick atmosphere and methane lakes
iapetus: Moon of the ringed planet with one dark side and one bright side
